Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider the properties of one-hot encoding. When you one-hot encode a categorical variable with \( $$n$$ \) categories, you typically create \( $$n-1$$ \) binary columns to avoid multicollinearity. However, in this problem, all categories are encoded, which might affect the invertibility of the matrix.

**Hint 2:** Recall that for a matrix to be invertible, it must be full rank. This means that none of the columns can be a linear combination of the others. Think about how the inclusion of an intercept term and the full one-hot encoding of categorical variables might impact the rank of the design matrix \(\Phi_2\).
